name: China economy
value: Shimao default (Oct); Huafa cut to junk 9 Nov
summary: Developer defaults persist: Shimao defaulted in Oct, a Zhongrong unit faces liquidation, state-owned Huafa cut to junk
state: Shimao defaulted again in October despite an earlier restructuring, a Hong Kong court ordered the liquidation of Zhongrong Real Estate's core subsidiary on 9 Nov, and Fitch cut Zhuhai's state-owned Huafa Group two notches to BB+ the same day (TechNews, 19 Nov). October data showed consumer prices up 0.7% on the year (NBS) and retail sales, industrial output and investment all slowing (SCMP, 16 Nov). Renewed developer defaults meet the Watch line; there is no hard landing, wider financial contagion or capital-control tightening.
for_you: Businesses that trade with China may see weaker demand and payment delays from property-linked firms. Effects abroad so far are limited.
rubric_hit: Renewed property-developer defaults (Shimao, Zhongrong) = Watch; no hard landing or contagion

sources.title: TechNews — Zhuhai Huafa could become China's next real estate flashpoint

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
